brief: BofA argues the Fed cannot credibly hold at the September 16 FOMC. Markets price over 80bp of hikes over 12 months, oil has broken $100/bbl, and the ECB hiked 25bp on September 10 while the BoJ is expected to hike 25bp next week, so the Fed, which faces the strongest economy and highest core inflation of the big three, would be read as committing a policy error if it stayed on hold. August PPI was firmer than expected, lifting BofA August core PCE tracking to 0.26% m/m from 0.24%, which the note says greenlights a hike. August CPI had not printed at the time of writing and a very soft print is the stated escape. If the Fed does not hike, BofA sees long-end yields rising through breakeven inflation and term premium. It expects 25bp hikes in September, October and December, a 2026 median dot implying 50bp this year and a 2027 median showing one cut. Growth is solid at 2.6% 3Q tracking, the labour market is in balance at 77k monthly job growth, and underlying inflation is stuck near 2.5%.
